title: Introduction to Complex Numbers: Lecture 1 - Oxford Mathematics 1st Year Student Lecture
description:
Introduction to Complex Numbers: Lecture 1 - Oxford Mathematics 1st Year Student Lecture
Oxford Mathematics
729000 subscribers
5917 likes
194863 views
1 Dec 2024
To make sure our students, who come from all over the world, are up to speed for the challenges ahead, this lecture recaps much of the work they should have done at high school, providing a short description of some of the basics of complex numbers.

But even in an recap there are subtle differences and pointers to what's to come.

You can watch the subsequent lecture (from a few years ago) here: https://youtu.be/BP7Ujbyu-NE

You can watch many other student lectures via our main Student Lectures playlist (also check out specific student lectures playlists): https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PL4d5ZtfQonW0A4VHeiY0gSkX1QEraaacE

All first and second year lectures are followed by tutorials where students meet their tutor in pairs to go through the lecture and associated problem sheet and to talk and think more about the maths. Third and fourth year lectures are followed by classes.

title: Undergraduate Lecture Notes Oxford University : r/math
description: # Undergraduate Lecture Notes Oxford University : r/math. Skip to main contentUndergraduate Lecture Notes Oxford University : r/math. # Undergraduate Lecture Notes Oxford University. In my search for study materials for my own math degree, I found the official website for the math courses at Oxford. Under the banner "Undergraduate Courses" you can find almost all math courses, that are taught at Oxford and following the course link, most of the time you will find the course materials including the lecture notes and some problem sets. How is the math program at Oxford actually structured (which of the courses are compulsory) and is Part A actually the first year? From my experience as a german student, the first 2 years of the math degree are pretty much the same at every university, so the Part A courses appear more like 2nd year courses to me.
